💡 RelateAnything | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Predicting relationships between objects in images or video frames using flexible, user-defined vocabularies and without relying on predefined object class labels.
✨ Key Features: • Real-time open-vocabulary relation prediction • Predicate vocabulary supplied at inference (no retraining needed)
📖 Summary: RelateAnything is a Python library for real-time, open-vocabulary relation prediction from any input. It allows users to define custom relation predicates at inference time without retraining, and it does not require object class labels, making it highly flexible. The model can output ranked lists of relations, or both spatial and semantic graphs simultaneously.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ openGym | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a private, self-hosted fitness tracking solution that gives them full control over their workout data and progress.
✨ Key Features: • Self-hosted fitness tracker • Body-weight tracking with interactive charts • Workout logging (supersets, warm-ups, cardio)
📖 Summary: openGym is a self-hosted, progressive web application for tracking gym workouts and body weight. It allows users to plan routines, log sets, supersets, warm-ups, and cardio, while also visualizing muscle fatigue and training progress. The application emphasizes data ownership and privacy, offering features like passkey login and import capabilities from other fitness apps.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 Thingport | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Centralizing and managing a personal collection of 3D models from multiple online sources.
✨ Key Features: • Personal model library • Import from model websites • Search & organize • 3D previews • Archive your models
📖 Summary: Thingport is a self-hosted web application designed to help 3D printing enthusiasts collect, organize, preview, and manage their 3D models from various online platforms. It provides a centralized library to prevent collections from becoming disorganized.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ maxun | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To enable users to extract, automate, search, and monitor data from any website by converting it into a structured API.
✨ Key Features: • Real-time web scraping • Web crawling • Web search • Website monitoring • AI data extraction
📖 Summary: Maxun is an open-source web data platform designed for real-time web scraping, crawling, search, monitoring, and AI-driven data extraction. It allows users to transform any website into a structured API, enabling automation and efficient data retrieval.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 telegram-mcp | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To enable AI assistants and other MCP-compatible clients to interact with and manage Telegram accounts, chats, and messages through a standardized protocol.
✨ Key Features: • Exposes Telegram account, chat, message, contact, media, folder, and admin operations via MCP • Supports sending, scheduling, editing, deleting, forwarding, pinning, and searching messages
📖 Summary: Telegram MCP Server is a Python-based server that bridges Telegram with Model Context Protocol (MCP) compatible clients like Claude and Cursor. It allows these clients to interact with Telegram features such as reading chats, managing groups, sending and modifying messages, and handling media and contacts.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source
